web.title: Medicare Levy Surcharge - Private Healthcare Australia (PHA)
web.description:
**What is the Medicare Levy Surcharge (MLS)?**

The Medicare Levy Surcharge is an extra 1% to 1.5% levy paid by Australian taxpayers who don’t have Private Hospital Cover and are considered by the Government to be high income earners.

The Medicare Levy Surcharge is in addition to the 2% Medicare levy (which is paid by most Australian taxpayers) and aims to encourage individuals to take out Private Hospital Cover. The Medicare Levy Surcharge currently applies to those Australian taxpayers who do not have private hospital cover and who earn above $105,000 for individuals and $210,000 for couples or families, increasing by $1,500 for each dependent child after the first.

**Currently, you have to pay the surcharge if you are:**

- a single person with an annual taxable income for MLS purposes greater than $101,000 in the 2025-26 financial year or greater than $105,000 in the 2026-27 financial year; or
- a family or couple with a combined taxable income for MLS purposes greater than $202,000 in the 2025-26 financial year or greater than $210,000 in the 2026-27 financial year. The family income threshold increases by $1,500 for each dependent child after the first;

The table below shows the income thresholds and MLS rates set by the Australian Government for the 2026-27 financial year.

| Singles | $105,000 or less | $105,001 – $123,000 | $123,001 – $164,000 | $164,001 or more |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| Families | $210,000 or less | $210,001 – $246,000 | $246,001 – $328,000 | $328,001 or more |
|  | **Base Tier** | **Tier 1** | **Tier 2** | **Tier 3** |
| ### MEDICARE LEVY SURCHARGE |
| All ages | 0.0% | 1.0% | 1.25% | 1.5% |

_**Notes:**_

- _The thresholds increase annually, based on growth in Average Weekly Ordinary Time Earnings (AWOTE). Single parents and couples (including de facto couples) are subject to the family tiers. For families with children, the thresholds are increased by $1,500 for each dependent child after the first._
- For the period of 1 July 2015 to 30 June 2023, the income tiers were paused at the 2014-15 threshold levels. For the thresholds applicable from 2010-11 to 2026-27, go to the [ATO website](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy-surcharge/medicare-levy-surcharge-income-thresholds-and-rates).

Further Medicare Levy Surcharge (MLS) information is available from the [Australian Taxation Office (ATO) website](https://www.ato.gov.au/Individuals/Medicare-and-private-health-insurance/Medicare-levy-surcharge/)

web.description:
# M2 Medicare levy surcharge 2026
## Things you need to know
### Medicare levy surcharge income testing
We income test the MLS against the following income tier thresholds.

Income thresholds

**Note:** The family income threshold increases by $1,500 for each [MLS dependant child](https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/individual-tax-return-2026-instructions/medicare-levy-questions-m1-m2-individual-tax-return-2026/m2-medicare-levy-surcharge-2026#Dependants) after the first child.

You may have to pay MLS for any period during the income year when both of the following apply:

- your income for MLS purposes was above the threshold.

### Income for MLS purposes
Your income for MLS purposes was your taxable income (excluding any assessable [first home super saver](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/withdrawing-and-using-your-super/early-access-to-super/first-home-super-saver-scheme) released amount) _plus_ the following if they applied to you:

## What you need to answer this question
### Surcharge exemption categories
- You were **single** for the **whole of 2025–26**, and both of the following apply:
  - your income for MLS purposes was **$101,000 or less**.
- You were **single** for the **whole of 2025–26**, and
  - your income for MLS purposes was **$202,000 or less** ( _plus_ $1,500 for each dependant child after the first).
- You were **single** for **part of 2025–26**, and
  - your income for MLS purposes was **$101,000 or less**.
- You had a **spouse** (with or without dependant children) **for the whole of 2025–26**, and your combined income for MLS purposes was either
  - **$202,000 or less** ( _plus_ $1,500 for each dependant child after the first)
  - **greater than $202,000** ( _plus_ $1,500 for each dependant child after the first) but your own income for MLS purposes is **$28,011 or less**.

### Income threshold when your circumstances change during the year
We will calculate the rate of your MLS liability using either:

- your own income for MLS purposes is more than **$101,000**

#### Example: spouse for the first part of the year
- Michelle is liable to pay MLS for this period because her $102,000 income for MLS purposes exceeded $101,000
- Michael isn't liable for MLS for this period because his $69,000 income for MLS purposes was less than $101,000.

In calculating the rate of MLS levied on Michelle, the single income threshold is used as Michelle was single on 30 June 2026. Michelle's own income for MLS purposes is $102,000, which is above the single tier 1 threshold ($101,000). This means that any MLS levied on Michelle is at the tier 1 rate of 1%. Therefore, Michelle's MLS for the second part of the year is calculated as follows:

**$102,000 × 1% × (262 ÷ 365) = $732.16**

#### Example: spouse for the second part of the year
In calculating the rate of MLS levied on Alice, the family income threshold is used as Alice was married on 30 June 2026. Alice and Adam's combined income for MLS purposes is $239,000, which is above the family tier 2 earner threshold ($236,000). This means that any surcharge levied on Alice is at the rate of 1.25%. Therefore, Alice's MLS for the first part of the year is calculated as follows:

**$142,000 (taxable income) × 1.25% × (200 ÷ 365) = $972.60**

web.title: Medicare Levy Surcharge 2026–27: What is it and who has to pay? - Etax
web.description:
## Key Takeaways
- The Medicare Levy Surcharge (MLS) is separate from the Medicare Levy and only applies to high-income Australians without private hospital cover.
- For 2026–27, the surcharge kicks in at $105,001 for singles and $210,001 for families.

## How is the Medicare Levy Surcharge calculated?
### Medicare Levy Surcharge income tiers for the 2026–27 financial year:
|  |  |  |  |  |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| Income Threshold | Base Tier | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 |
| **Single** | Up to $105,000 | $105,001 – $123,000 | $123,001 – $164,000 | $164,001 or more |
| **Family** | Up to $210,000 | $210,001 – $246,000 | $246,001 – $328,000 | $328,001 or more |
| **Medicare levy surcharge** | 0% | 1% | 1.25% | 1.5% |

The family income threshold is increased by $1,500 for each MLS dependent child after the first child.

### Medicare Levy Surcharge income tiers for the 2025–26 financial year:
|  |  |  |  |  |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| Income Threshold | Income | Income | Income | Income |
| **Single** | Up to $101,000 | $101,001 – $118,000 | $118,001 – $158,000 | $158,001 or more |
| **Family** | Up to $202,000 | $202,001 – $236,000 | $236,001 – $316,000 | $316,001 or more |
| **Medicare levy surcharge** | 0% | 1% | 1.25% | 1.5% |

The family income threshold is increased by $1,500 for each MLS dependent child after the first child.

- [See Earlier Years](https://www.etax.com.au/medicare-levy-surcharge/#Earlier-years)

## Earlier Medicare Levy Surcharge thresholds:
### Medicare Levy Surcharge income tiers for 2024–25 financial year are:
- $97,001 – $113,000 – the surcharge is 1% of your income
- $113,001 – $151,000 – the surcharge is 1.25% of your income
- $151,001 and above – the surcharge is 1.5% of your income

- $194,001 – $226,000 – the surcharge is 1% of your combined income
- $226,001 – $302,000 – the surcharge is 1.25% of your combined income
- $302,001 and above – the surcharge is 1.5% of your combined income

### The income tiers for _individuals_ for 2023–24 financial year are:
- $93,000 – $108,000 – the surcharge is 1% of your income
- $108,001 – $144,000 – the surcharge is 1.25% of your income
- $144,001 and above – the surcharge is 1.5% of your income

### The income tiers for _families_ for 2023–24 financial year are:
For both 2024–25 and 2023–24, the family income threshold is increased by $1,500 for each MLS dependent child after the first child.

# Medicare levy calculator
**Last updated** 1 July 2026

## What you can do with this calculator
For most taxpayers the [Medicare levy](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy) is 2% of their taxable income.

You may have to pay MLS for any period during the income year when both of the following apply:

- your income for MLS purposes is above the threshold.

If you have to pay the Medicare levy, you may have to pay the Medicare levy surcharge (MLS).

If applicable, we will include MLS with your Medicare levy.

## What you will need
- Your taxable income.

web.title: Medicare Levy Surcharge Explained - H&R Block
web.description:
# What is the Medicare Levy Surcharge?
By [H&R Block](https://www.hrblock.com.au/) 7 min read

Last updated: 22 May 2026

Originally published: Jul 2020

For 2025–26, it affects singles earning over $101,000 and families over $202,000, with rates of 1% to 1.5%. For the 2026-27 year, this threshold will increase to $105,000 for singles and $210,000 for families. To avoid the surcharge, qualifying hospital cover must be held for the entire income year, as extras-only policies do not count.

![Medicare levy surcharge explained for Australian taxpayers, including income thresholds, surcharge rates and private hospital cover requirements](https://www.hrblock.com.au/getattachment/9478511d-aa92-4dd8-bbf2-4222ca5f8b73/iStock-825409934.jpg)

The Medicare levy surcharge (MLS) is an additional tax that may apply if you earn above certain income thresholds and do not have an appropriate level of private patient hospital cover for the full financial year.

The Medicare levy surcharge is separate from the standard Medicare levy, which is generally 2% of taxable income and paid by most Australian taxpayers.

## Income Thresholds and Surcharge Rates
### 2025–26 Income Year (1 July 2025–30 June 2026)
|  |  |  |  |  |
|-|-|-|-|-|
|  | Base Tier | Tier1 | Tier2 | Tier 3 |
| Singles | $101,000 or less | $101,001-$118,000 | $118,001-$158,000 | $158,001 or more |
| Families | $202,000 or less | $202,001-$236,000 | $236,001-$316,000 | $316,001 or more |
| Medicare levy surcharge rate | 0% | 1% | 1.25% | 1.5% |

For family thresholds, the income level increases by $1,500 for each dependent child after the first.

### 2026–27 Income Year (1 July 2026–30 June 2027)
These thresholds are similar but start at higher income levels:

|  |  |  |  |  |
|-|-|-|-|-|
|  | Base Tier | Tier1 | Tier2 | Tier 3 |
| Singles | $105,000 or less | $105,001-$123,000 | $123,001-$164,000 | $164,001 or more |
| Families | $210,000 or less | $210,001-$246,000 | $246,001-$328,000 | $328,001 or more |
| Medicare levy surcharge rate | 0% | 1% | 1.25% | 1.5% |

Family thresholds again increase for dependants after the first.

### Income Thresholds for Surcharge Purposes
|  |  |  |  |  |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| Singles | $101,000 or less | $101,001 - $118,000 | $118,001 - $158,000 | $158,001 + |
| Families (no. of children: 0-1) | $202,000 or less | $202,001 - $236,000 | $236,001 - $316,000 | $316,001 + |
| Families (no. of children: 2) | $203,500 or less | $203,501 - $237,500 | $237,501 - $317,500 | $317,501 + |
| Families (no. of children: 3) | $205,000 or less | $205,001 - $239,000 | $239,001 - $319,000 | $319,001 + |
| Families (no. of children: 4) | $206,500 or less | $206,501 - $240,500 | $240,501 -$320,500 | $320,501 + |
| MLS rate | 0% | 1% | 1.25% | 1.5% |

We can help you work out your income for MLS purposes and check whether the surcharge applies based on your circumstances.

## What Counts as Income for MLS Purposes?
- Taxable income
- Reportable fringe benefits
- Net investment loss (including rental property losses)
- Reportable superannuation contributions
- If applicable, certain trust income and exempt foreign employment income

## Frequently asked questions about the Medicare levy surcharge
##### #### What income is used to calculate the Medicare levy surcharge?
The Medicare levy surcharge is based on your income for surcharge purposes, not just your taxable income. This can include taxable income, reportable fringe benefits, reportable superannuation contributions, and net investment losses. If you have a spouse, their income is also included when working out family income for MLS purposes.
